content.title: UFL announces new teams in Louisville, Orlando and Columbus
content.text: Houston, Dallas-area teams also rebranded, moving venues within marketsThe newly announced lineup of markets and brands in the United Football League. New cities include Columbus, Louisville and Orlando. UFL teams 2026 The United Football League will launch new teams in Louisville and Orlando alongside a previously announced new club in Columbus in 2026, replacing Memphis, Detroit and San Antonio in the eight-team league.The spring league also announced two other team brand changes as it reorganizes under the leadership of new investor Mike Repole: The Houston Roughnecks will now revert to the old USFL branding, the Houston Gamblers, and will move from Univ. of Houston’s TDECU Stadium to Shell Energy Stadium in downtown. Also in Texas, the Arlington Renegades will leave Choctaw Stadium for Toyota Stadium and be renamed the Dallas Renegades.But the changes are as much about venues as markets or brands. The UFL’s five newly rebranded teams -- The Columbus Aviators, the Louisville Kings, the Orlando Storm, the Houston Gamblers, and the Dallas Renegades -- will all play in soccer-specific stadiums with capacities of 25,000 or lower.This is a big step toward Repole’s goal of rationalizing the UFL’s realistic attendance expectations with venue size, after he observed poor fan experience in stadiums that are less than one-quarter full. In 2025, the average UFL game drew 12,162 fans, but the average venue held more than 52,000. In an interview, Repole acknowledged Memphis simply never performed well by any measurement, but San Antonio and Detroit’s main problem was the lack of an appropriately sized venue. “San Antonio has a really, really good fan base, there were no venues that were more than 7,000, and the stadium just didn’t work,” Repole said. “The Alamodome, with 70,000 people, and only having 11,000 fans at a game, it looked like a COVID game, same thing with Michigan and Ford Field.”He didn’t rule out returning to Detroit once the USL’s Detroit City FC planned downtown soccer stadium is finished. Columbus, Louisville and Orlando are all large, football-centric markets with limited other pro sports options and well-suited soccer stadiums, he said. “What I love about these soccer venues, you are right in the middle of the action, there isn’t a bad seat in the house,” Repole said. The venue agreements are multiyear deals, the league said.Including the D.C. Defenders, who have played in the MLS Audi Field since founding, six of the eight UFL teams in 2026 will play in MLS or USL stadiums. Only the Birmingham Stallions (Protective Stadium, 47,100) and the St. Louis Battlehawks (The Dome at America’s Center, 67,500) will still play in football-first venues. St. Louis is by far the league’s best-drawing team, averaging more than 29,500 fans last year.Repole hopes the two remaining Texas teams will see a surge in interest by playing in downtown soccer venues. He felt the Gamblers (original USFL name) had more brand equity than the Roughnecks (XFL branding.)“The Houston Gamblers are iconic,” he said. “People know them, and I think moving downtown, people will see it as a new team.”Sponsored contentAdditional SectionsAwards & HonorsBettingCollegesDataEvents and Attractions Exec TransactionsFacilitiesFinanceFranchisesInternationalLabor and AgentsLeagues and Governing BodiesLegal and GovernanceMarketingMediaOlympicsOpinionPeople and Pop CultureSports and SocietyTechWomen's SportsSBJ TV
